analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 1–801 against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. The visible substantive change at lines 684–691 replaces separate weight-hashing passes with the verified manifest aggregate and permits restart registration from cached file identities; it explicitly retains verification before serving. This affects A-004, T-012, T-027 and the TB-002 routing contract, but the documentation alone establishes neither a verification bypass nor a concrete regression. Integration should examine GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256, ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and VerifiedWeightHashStore for complete inventory binding, construction-time mutation detection, cache invalidation and compatibility with coordinator weight-hash expectations, including whether cached registration can affect routing before load verification.
Surrounding text describes authenticated cache scopes and cold fallback without scope (232–238, 528–529), reservation-before-media-decode and bounded cancellation (95–145), retained charges on native faults (553–565, 649–661), and GLM admission/publication limits (746–790). These controls were considered for confidentiality, availability and billing interactions; their unchanged documentation is not evidence of a new regression. The resident prefix bank differs from T-041's SSD-only wording, but the supplied complete change ranges show that description is unchanged, so it is not attributed to this PR. No visible change affects attestation, serving authorization, hop encryption, token custody or privileged fan authority. Later changed sections of this document are outside these units; the truncated patch does not provide enough evidence to review them here. Implementation validation of the new cached-weight identity contract remains necessary.
